entries.note: The extracted proposition evaluates the valuation's reasonableness.
The central assertion concerns deliberate leaking, a private intention. The separate assertion about matching dates is publicly checkable.

entries.test: Public acquisition offers, IPO preparations, and financial records would show whether acquisition or public listing was a viable exit for most AI startups at publication.
entries.note: The bubble metaphor accompanies a substantive claim about available exits.
Being the entire bubble's 'weak point' has no shared measure or decisive test.

entries.test: Cursor's subsequent subscription cancellations, annualized revenue, and fundraising results would show whether the service changes produced the predicted decline.
entries.note: This is a firm forecast with a causal explanation and no deadline.

entries.test: Claude Code churn following the weekly limits, compared with historically extreme SaaS churn rates, would test the prediction.
entries.note: 'Will, I believe' expresses a firm prediction; 'gnarly' plainly means exceptionally severe churn.

entries.test: Anthropic's financing disclosures, Amazon infrastructure obligations, and operating cash requirements would show whether it needed the fundraising to pay Amazon to continue serving its models.
entries.note: Paying Andy Jassy is figurative language for paying Amazon. The assessment of model quality is evaluative.
The central claim is a judgment of worth, supported by an assertion about losses.

entries.test: Public records of generative AI acquisitions through publication would establish their frequency and the proportion structured as acqui-hires or distressed sales.
entries.note: The colorful adjectives do not erase the factual characterization of completed deals.

entries.test: Publicly reported bids and acquisition negotiations would show whether buyers demonstrated willingness to purchase comparable generative AI companies at roughly $9.9 billion.
entries.note: Investor hunger has a plain commercial reading as demonstrated acquisition demand.

entries.test: Generative AI startups' revenue, operating expenses, cash flows, and funding records at publication would show whether continued venture funding was necessary for survival.
entries.note: The funding-dependence assertion is factual even though 'impressive' is evaluative.

entries.test: Public unit economics, infrastructure costs, margins, and addressable-market estimates would permit comparison with the earlier cash-burning businesses discussed in the post.
entries.note: The surrounding paragraph supplies the comparison group, including Uber.

entries.test: Public evidence of application companies' proprietary assets and their ability to switch models or withstand provider price changes and competition would test the asserted permanent dependence.
entries.note: In context this concerns companies building on external model providers. 'Forever' supplies no finite deadline.

entries.test: Perplexity's founding and funding records, operating losses, margins, and financial trajectory at publication would show whether it was approaching profitability.
entries.note: The financial assessment has a plain reading despite the hedge.

entries.test: OpenAI's cash-flow records for approximately June through early August 2025 would establish whether it burned at least $10 billion.
entries.note: Fundraising amounts alone would not establish cash burn.
'Does not make sense' evaluates the projection without specifying an alternative outcome. The fundraising schedule is separately checkable.
The post itself calls 'essential' subjective and supplies no shared threshold. The Copilot comparison also lacks a defined set of capabilities.
This attributes a private motive for OpenAI's disclosure choices.

entries.test: Public financial results, acquisition offers relative to valuations, and disclosed intellectual-property assets would test the asserted losses, limited revenues, and lack of commercially valuable assets.
entries.note: This bundles several claims; its concrete financial assertions remain checkable despite evaluative wording.
The Microsoft outcome is explicitly described as the most likely scenario.
The extracted conclusion about desperation is a rhetorical characterization. The offer's price and availability are separately checkable.

entries.test: Public deployment and usage evidence would show whether LLM use ultimately contracts to costly enthusiast hardware and a small number of niche enterprise applications.
entries.note: 'I think ... will' presents a substantive expected outcome without a deadline.
The quantified loss is explicitly only possible. The separate assertion that the current product form can never become profitable is firmer.
'Cannot imagine' expresses doubt about the hypothetical customer response rather than a firm outcome.

entries.test: The Magnificent Seven's reported capital expenditures for January through June 2025 would establish whether their combined spending exceeded $200 billion.
entries.note: The period had already ended when the post appeared. 'I expect' is not disqualifying probability language.

entries.test: Kedrosky's estimate methodology and public 2025 AI capital-spending records would show whether omitted Oracle and private-developer spending made the estimate an underestimate.
entries.note: Here 'too conservative' means numerically too low because of identified omissions.

entries.test: CoreWeave's reported losses, subsequent profitability, and ability to continue operating through a market downturn would test the asserted lack of a viable path.
entries.note: The market-downturn condition specifically qualifies continued operation; the profitability assessment is broader.
Both 'may ultimately' and 'will likely' explicitly qualify the outcomes as possibilities or probabilities.
Anthropic's fate without those investments is a counterfactual. Actual investment amounts and 2025 losses are separately checkable.

entries.test: Tech-sector employment and offshoring records following an AI investment bust and capex decline, alongside corporate cost-cutting disclosures, would show whether layoffs and offshoring accelerated for fiscal reasons.
entries.note: The preceding paragraphs supply the trigger. 'First time in living memory' is rhetorical embellishment.

entries.test: Venture funding totals, pension investment losses, and resulting retirement-income changes following an AI bust would test the predicted financial contraction.
entries.note: The condition is supplied by the surrounding discussion; 'grim' is an accompanying judgment.

entries.test: Data-center utilization, operating income, and asset impairments after the described AI bust would show whether the affected facilities became non-performing assets.
entries.note: The normalization broadens 'these data centers' to AI data centers generally and drops the surrounding bust scenario. The opportunity-cost language is not a precise measurable prediction.
'Hard to imagine' expresses doubt, and the statement explicitly considers the condition of eventual profitability.
This expresses dread without specifying a testable disaster, trigger, or horizon.
